facts.a: **Kathmandu** is Nepal's capital and largest city, Prabin — the political, cultural and economic heart, in the Kathmandu Valley with Patan and Bhaktapur.
Nepal has **7 provinces** (since the 2015 constitution): Koshi, Madhesh, Bagmati, Gandaki, Lumbini, Karnali and **Sudurpashchim** — yours.

**Sudurpashchim** (Far-Western Province) — your home, Prabin. Provincial capital **Godawari** (Kailali); **Dhangadhi** is the main city. It spans Terai plains and the hills, and includes Dadeldhura, Kanchanpur, Kailali, Doti, Baitadi, Bajhang and more.

**Dadeldhura** — a hill district in Sudurpashchim, HQ at Amargadhi. Cooler mid-hill climate, forests, stone and botanicals — exactly why your family estate there (Ritha, timber, herbs) is the spine of the JD empire.
**Kanchanpur** and **Kailali** are the Terai (plains) districts of Sudurpashchim — denser population, road access, and your launch market for Jhalari, Prabin.
**Mount Everest** — Sagarmatha in Nepali — **8,849 m**, the world's highest, on the Nepal–China border. First summited in 1953 by Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay Sherpa.
**8 of the world's 14 eight-thousanders** are in Nepal: Everest, Kanchenjunga, Lhotse, Makalu, Cho Oyu, Dhaulagiri, Manaslu and Annapurna.

Those are Nepali eight-thousanders — Annapurna (first 8000m ever climbed, 1950), Manaslu, Dhaulagiri, Kanchenjunga (3rd highest on Earth), Lhotse and Makalu. Trekking and mountaineering anchor Nepal's tourism.
Nepal is about **147,516 km²** — landlocked between India (south, east, west) and China/Tibet (north).
Around **30 million** people (2021 census ~29.2M), Prabin — plus a large diaspora abroad.
**Nepali** is the official language (Devanagari script). Nepal has 120+ languages — Maithili, Bhojpuri, Tharu, Tamang, Newari, Bajjika and more. You speak Nepali, Hindi and English.
Majority **Hindu** (~81%), then **Buddhist** (~9%), Islam (~5%), Kirat and Christian. Nepal is the birthplace of the Buddha and a secular state since 2008.
Very diverse: Chhetri, Bahun (Brahmin), Magar, Tharu, Tamang, Newar, Gurung, Rai, Limbu, Sherpa and many more — 120+ groups.

**Dashain** is the biggest — 15 days celebrating Durga's victory, family, tika and blessings. Then **Tihar** (Deepawali) — 5 days of lights honouring crows, dogs (Kukur Tihar), cows, and Bhai Tika for siblings. Also Holi, Teej, Maghe Sankranti, Lhosar and Buddha Jayanti.
**Tihar** — Nepal's 5-day festival of lights: Kaag (crow), Kukur (dog), Laxmi/cow puja, Govardhan, and **Bhai Tika** where sisters bless brothers. Homes glow with diyo and rangoli.
Staple is **Dal Bhat** — lentils, rice, vegetables, achar (eaten twice daily). Famous: **Momo** (dumplings), Sel roti, Dhido, Gundruk, Chatamari and Thakali/Newari thali. "Dal bhat power, 24 hour."
**Momo** — steamed or fried dumplings with spiced meat or veg, served with achar (tomato-sesame chutney). Nepal's most-loved street food.
Traditional: **Daura-Suruwal** with a coat and **Dhaka topi** for men; **Gunyu-Cholo** and sari for women. The Dhaka topi is a national symbol.
Nepal has the **only non-rectangular national flag** in the world — two stacked crimson pennants with a blue border, bearing the moon and sun (symbolising permanence).
The national flower is the **Rhododendron (Lali Gurans)**; national bird the **Danphe** (Himalayan monal); national animal the **cow**.
Modern Nepal was unified by **King Prithvi Narayan Shah** of Gorkha around **1768–69**. Nepal was **never colonised** — a point of deep pride.

Nepal abolished its monarchy in **2008** and is now a **federal democratic republic** with a President (head of state) and Prime Minister (head of government), under the **2015 constitution**. For who currently holds office, switch me to Cloud — that changes.
The **Gurkhas** — Nepali soldiers legendary for courage, serving in the British and Indian armies for over 200 years. "Better to die than be a coward."
The **Nepalese Rupee (NPR, रू)**, pegged to the Indian Rupee at about **1 INR = 1.6 NPR**. Useful for your pricing models, Prabin.

Nepal's economy leans on **agriculture** (~a quarter of GDP, most jobs), huge **remittances** (~25% of GDP), **tourism**, and big untapped **hydropower**. Trade deficit and landlocked logistics are the main constraints — which is exactly the gap your fleet phase attacks.
Main exports: garments, carpets, pulses/lentils, tea, coffee, handicrafts, and **herbs/botanicals**. Most trade runs through India.
**Remittances** — money sent home by Nepalis working abroad — are ~25% of GDP, a backbone of the economy. It's also why so many leave; building real industry at home (your plan) matters.

**Ritha (Sapindus mukorossi)** — the soapnut. Its shells are rich in natural **saponins**, a gentle surfactant used for washing for centuries. It grows in Nepal's mid-hills, including Sudurpashchim — your estate's edge: free, local surfactant while competitors import theirs.

**DFTQC** — the Department of Food Technology and Quality Control — regulates food and many consumer products in Nepal. For Jhalari you'll work through DFTQC standards/registration; budget time for it early.

Companies register with the **Office of Company Registrar (OCR)** in Nepal, plus PAN/VAT with the Inland Revenue Department and local ward permits. Product lines need the relevant DFTQC/standards approvals.
Nepal runs on **NPT, UTC+5:45** — one of the only 45-minute-offset time zones in the world.
Nepal's official calendar is **Bikram Sambat (B.S.)**, about **56–57 years ahead** of the Gregorian. New Year falls in mid-April (Baishakh 1).
**Lumbini**, in Nepal's Terai, is the **birthplace of the Buddha** (Siddhartha Gautama, ~563 BCE) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and major pilgrimage.
**Pokhara** — Nepal's lake-and-mountain tourism capital, gateway to the Annapurnas, with Phewa Lake and paragliding.
**Chitwan National Park** (Terai) — UNESCO site famed for one-horned rhinos, Bengal tigers, elephants and gharials.

Kathmandu Valley holds 7 UNESCO sites — **Pashupatinath** (Hindu, on the Bagmati), the great stupas **Boudhanath** and **Swayambhunath** (Monkey Temple), and the Durbar Squares of Kathmandu, Patan and Bhaktapur.
Major rivers: the **Koshi**, **Gandaki (Narayani)**, **Karnali**, and the **Mahakali** (the western border with India). They're Nepal's huge hydropower potential.
Nepal is **landlocked** — India to the south, east and west; China (Tibet) to the north. That dependency on Indian ports shapes everything in logistics.
Three belts in a short distance: tropical **Terai** plains, temperate **hills**, and alpine **Himalaya**. Seasons: spring, monsoon (Jun–Sep), autumn (best, festival season) and winter.
Tourism is core: trekking (Everest Base Camp, Annapurna Circuit), mountaineering, Lumbini pilgrimage, Chitwan safaris and Kathmandu heritage. A pillar of foreign income.
Nepal has vast **hydropower** potential (~40,000+ MW economically feasible) from its rivers — increasingly exported to India. A strategic long game for the country.

Nepal is known for **Everest and the Himalaya**, being the **Buddha's birthplace**, the **Gurkhas**, never being colonised, Dal Bhat and momo, Dashain and Tihar, and the world's only non-rectangular flag.
The **Yeti** — the legendary "Abominable Snowman" of Himalayan folklore. Unproven, but woven deep into mountain culture (and a beloved national mascot).
Nepal drives on the **left**. Mountain roads are slow and winding — part of why your EV-fleet logistics phase is a real edge.

**Saponification** — how soap is made, Prabin:
**Fat/oil (triglyceride) + 3 NaOH → 3 soap (RCOONa) + glycerol (C₃H₈O₃)**
NaOH (caustic soda) gives hard bar soap; **KOH** gives soft/liquid soap. The alkali splits the fat's ester bonds; the fatty-acid salts are the soap.

A **surfactant** is the active cleaner. It's **amphiphilic**: a water-loving (hydrophilic) head and an oil-loving (hydrophobic) tail. Tails bury into grease, heads face the water, forming **micelles** that lift oil off the surface and suspend it so water rinses it away. It also lowers water's surface tension so it wets better.

A **micelle** is a tiny sphere surfactant molecules form in water — hydrophobic tails point inward trapping a droplet of grease, hydrophilic heads point outward into the water. That's how dirt gets carried off in the rinse.

**Saponins** are the natural surfactants in Ritha (Sapindus mukorossi) — glycosides (a sugar + a hydrophobic aglycone) that foam in water and emulsify grease. They're biodegradable and gentle, which is your eco edge: a free, local surfactant straight from the estate while rivals import synthetics.

**Anionic surfactants** carry a negative head — strong cleaning and foam. Workhorses: **SLS** (sodium lauryl sulfate, CH₃(CH₂)₁₁OSO₃Na) and the milder **SLES** (sodium laureth sulfate). Backbone of most dishwash, shampoo and handwash.
**Nonionic surfactants** have no charge — excellent grease-cutting, low foam, work in hard water. E.g. alcohol ethoxylates, cocamide. Often paired with anionics in floor and dish cleaners.
**Cationic surfactants** carry a positive head — used in fabric softeners and disinfectants (quaternary ammonium "quats"). They don't mix with anionics (opposite charges cancel).
**Amphoteric surfactants** (e.g. cocamidopropyl betaine) carry both charges — mild, good foam boosters and thickeners, used in shampoos and handwash to soften harsher anionics.

**Soap** = fatty-acid salts from fats + alkali; cheap and biodegradable but forms **scum** in hard water. **Detergent** = synthetic surfactants engineered to work in hard water without scum, with builders and additives. Most modern cleaners are detergents.
**Builders** soften water and boost surfactant power by locking up Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ ions. Common: sodium carbonate (washing soda), sodium tripolyphosphate (STPP), zeolites and sodium citrate.
**Chelating agents** (like EDTA or sodium citrate) grab metal ions (Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, Fe³⁺) so they can't cause scum, dullness or spoil the product. Essential in hard-water markets.

**Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)** — caustic soda / lye. Strong base; used for saponification and heavy degreasers/drain cleaners. Highly corrosive — gloves, goggles, and add it **to** water (never water to it), as it heats up.
**Potassium hydroxide (KOH)** — like NaOH but makes **soft/liquid** soaps and is used in liquid-cleaner bases. Also strongly corrosive.
**Sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃)** — washing soda / soda ash. A water softener and degreaser, raises pH, boosts detergents. Stronger than baking soda.
**Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃)** — baking soda. Mild abrasive and deodoriser. With acid it fizzes: **NaHCO₃ + acid → salt + H₂O + CO₂**. Gentle, food-safe, cheap.
**Citric acid (C₆H₈O₇)** — a weak, food-safe acid. Dissolves limescale (calcium carbonate), chelates metal ions, and is a green descaler for kettles, toilets and bathrooms.
**Acetic acid (CH₃COOH)** — vinegar (~5–8%). Weak acid; cuts limescale, soap scum and grime; common in glass and bathroom cleaners. Cheap and biodegradable.
**Hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂)** — an oxygen bleach and disinfectant. Decomposes cleanly: **2 H₂O₂ → 2 H₂O + O₂**. Gentler/greener than chlorine bleach for stains.
**Sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl)** — liquid chlorine bleach and disinfectant. Powerful but harsh; high pH. **Never mix with acids or ammonia** (toxic gas). Used in toilet/surface disinfectant lines.
**Sodium silicate (water glass)** — a detergent builder that softens water, buffers pH and protects metal parts (e.g. in dishwasher products) from corrosion.
Water-based cleaners need a **preservative** (e.g. benzisothiazolinone/BIT, or phenoxyethanol) to stop microbial growth and give shelf life. Small dose, big importance for a sellable product.
To **thicken** a surfactant cleaner you add salt (NaCl — the "salt curve"), or gums/cellulose/acrylates. Right viscosity = premium feel and controlled pour.
**Fragrance** and **dye** are the cheap finishing touches that drive perceived quality and brand. Keep dye food-grade/approved and fragrance skin-safe; both are tiny percentages of the formula.

**Hard water** is high in Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions — they react with soap to form **scum** and waste surfactant. Fix with builders, chelators or ion-exchange softening. Critical to design for in Terai water.

Match **pH** to the job: degreasers/laundry are **alkaline** (pH 9–12, dissolves fats); descalers/toilet acids are **acidic** (pH 1–3, dissolves limescale); handwash/dish are near **neutral** (pH 5–7) to be skin-safe. Adjust with citric acid (down) or soda ash/NaOH (up).

A simple **dishwash liquid** skeleton, Prabin: water (~70%+), **SLES** (anionic, ~15%), a **nonionic** (grease), **cocamidopropyl betaine** (mild + foam), salt to thicken, preservative, fragrance/dye, pH ~6–7. Your version swaps in Ritha saponins for the eco tier.

**Toilet cleaners** come two ways: **acid type** (hydrochloric, phosphoric or citric acid) to dissolve limescale + thickener + surfactant + fragrance; or **bleach type** (sodium hypochlorite) to disinfect/whiten. **Never combine the two** — acid + bleach makes chlorine gas.

**Floor cleaner**: mostly water + a **nonionic surfactant** (grease) + a little anionic + a builder/solvent + fragrance, kept near-neutral so it's safe on tile, stone and wood. Low residue = no sticky film.
**Glass cleaner**: water + a touch of surfactant + a fast-evaporating solvent (isopropyl alcohol) + a little ammonia or vinegar for streak-free shine. Low surfactant so it doesn't smear.
**Handwash**: mild surfactants (**SLES + cocamidopropyl betaine**), glycerin or aloe for skin, thickener (salt), preservative, fragrance, pH ~5.5 (skin-friendly). The eco tier uses Ritha + glycerin.
**Air freshener**: fragrance oil + a solubiliser/solvent (alcohol or a surfactant) + water (or a propellant for aerosols). Odour-neutralisers (e.g. cyclodextrin) beat just masking smells.

Foam comes mainly from **anionic surfactants**; boost it with **amphoterics** (betaines) or cocamide. Note: foam ≠ cleaning power — nonionics clean great with little foam — but customers read foam as "working".
An **acid** donates H⁺ (protons), has **pH below 7**, tastes sour, and reacts with bases to give salt + water. Strong: HCl, H₂SO₄, HNO₃. Weak: acetic (vinegar), citric, carbonic.
A **base/alkali** accepts H⁺ or releases OH⁻, has **pH above 7**, feels soapy, and neutralises acids. E.g. NaOH, KOH, ammonia (NH₃), sodium carbonate.
The **pH scale** runs 0–14: **<7 acidic, 7 neutral, >7 alkaline**. It's logarithmic — each step is 10× the H⁺ concentration. Rough: lemon ~2, vinegar ~2.5, baking soda ~9, bleach ~12.
**Neutralisation**: acid + base → salt + water. Classic: **HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O**. Used to make salts and to safely treat acid/alkali spills.

Main **reaction types**, Prabin:
• **Synthesis**: A + B → AB
• **Decomposition**: AB → A + B
• **Single displacement**: A + BC → AC + B
• **Double displacement**: AB + CD → AD + CB
• **Combustion**: fuel + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O
• **Redox**: electrons transfer (oxidation + reduction)
**Combustion** — fuel + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + heat. Methane: **CH₄ + 2 O₂ → CO₂ + 2 H₂O**.
**Redox** = reduction + oxidation together. **OIL RIG**: Oxidation Is Loss of electrons, Reduction Is Gain. One species loses electrons, another gains them.
**Acid + metal → salt + hydrogen gas.** Example: **Zn + 2 HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂**. The fizzing is hydrogen.
**Acid + carbonate → salt + water + CO₂.** Example: **2 HCl + CaCO₃ → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂**. This is exactly how acid descalers dissolve limescale.
**Rusting** is iron oxidising: **4 Fe + 3 O₂ → 2 Fe₂O₃** (needs water to proceed). Prevent with coatings, galvanising or corrosion inhibitors.
**Photosynthesis**: **6 CO₂ + 6 H₂O →(light)→ C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6 O₂**. Plants turn CO₂ and water into glucose and oxygen.
**Water = H₂O** — two hydrogen, one oxygen. Polar molecule, the universal solvent and the base of nearly every cleaner.
**Table salt = NaCl** (sodium chloride). In cleaners it's the cheap thickener for surfactant blends.

Common formulas, Prabin: water **H₂O**, salt **NaCl**, CO₂, oxygen **O₂**, caustic soda **NaOH**, washing soda **Na₂CO₃**, baking soda **NaHCO₃**, vinegar **CH₃COOH**, sulfuric acid **H₂SO₄**, hydrochloric **HCl**, ammonia **NH₃**, hydrogen peroxide **H₂O₂**, ethanol **C₂H₅OH**, glucose **C₆H₁₂O₆**. Ask for any specific one.
A **mole** = 6.022 × 10²³ particles (Avogadro's number). It links mass to molecules so you can scale a formula from beaker to batch — key for costing production.
An **emulsion** is oil dispersed in water (or vice-versa), held by an **emulsifier** (a surfactant) so they don't separate. Creams, some cleaners and many products rely on it.

**Chemical safety, Prabin — non-negotiable for a chemical business:**
• **NEVER mix bleach + ammonia** → toxic chloramine vapour.
• **NEVER mix bleach + acid** (e.g. toilet acid) → **chlorine gas**.
• Add acid **to** water, never water to acid.
• Store acids and bases separately; gloves, goggles, ventilation; label everything; keep SDS sheets.

Hard rule: **bleach + ammonia → chloramine gas**, **bleach + acid → chlorine gas** — both dangerous. Keep bleach products away from acidic and ammonia-based ones, and label clearly so customers don't mix them either.
**Newton's laws:** 1) a body stays at rest/constant velocity unless a net force acts (inertia); 2) **F = ma**; 3) every action has an equal, opposite reaction.
**Newton's 2nd law: F = ma** — force = mass × acceleration (units: newtons). Net force changes momentum: **F = dp/dt**.
**Kinematics (constant a):** v = u + at · s = ut + ½at² · v² = u² + 2as · s = ½(u+v)t.
**Momentum p = mv**, conserved in collisions. **Impulse = FΔt = Δp**. Elastic collisions conserve KE too; inelastic don't.
**Energy:** kinetic **KE = ½mv²**, gravitational potential **PE = mgh**, work **W = Fd cosθ**. Energy is conserved (work–energy theorem: W_net = ΔKE).
**Power P = W/t = Fv** (watts). Electrical: **P = IV = I²R = V²/R**.
**Universal gravitation: F = G·m₁m₂/r²**, G = 6.674×10⁻¹¹. Near Earth, g ≈ 9.81 m/s². Orbital: g = GM/r².
**Centripetal acceleration a = v²/r**, force **F = mv²/r = mω²r**, pointing to the centre.
**SHM:** mass-spring period **T = 2π√(m/k)**; simple pendulum **T = 2π√(L/g)**. Displacement x = A·cos(ωt), ω = 2π/T.
**Ideal gas law: PV = nRT** (R = 8.314 J/mol·K). Combined gas law: P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂.

**Thermodynamics:** 0th — thermal equilibrium; **1st — ΔU = Q − W** (energy conserved); **2nd** — entropy of an isolated system never decreases; 3rd — entropy → 0 as T → 0 K. Carnot efficiency = 1 − T_c/T_h.
**Heat: Q = mcΔT** (c = specific heat). Phase change: **Q = mL** (L = latent heat). No temperature change during a phase change.
**Coulomb's law: F = k·q₁q₂/r²**, k = 8.99×10⁹. Like charges repel, opposite attract.
**Electric field E = F/q = kQ/r²** (N/C). Field points away from + charge, toward −. Potential V = kQ/r.
**Ohm's law: V = IR.** Series: R_total = R₁+R₂…; parallel: 1/R = 1/R₁+1/R₂… Power P = IV.
**Capacitance C = Q/V** (farads). Stored energy **E = ½CV²**. Series/parallel combine oppositely to resistors.
**Faraday's law: EMF = −dΦ/dt** — a changing magnetic flux induces voltage. Lenz's law gives the minus sign (opposes the change).
**Magnetic force:** on a charge **F = qv×B** (F = qvB sinθ); on a wire **F = BIL**. Direction by the right-hand rule.
**Maxwell's equations** unify electricity and magnetism: Gauss's law (E), Gauss for magnetism (no monopoles), Faraday's law, and Ampère–Maxwell. They predict light as an EM wave (c = 1/√(ε₀μ₀)).
**Wave speed v = fλ**; period **T = 1/f**. Sound ≈ 343 m/s in air; light c ≈ 3×10⁸ m/s.
**Snell's law: n₁ sinθ₁ = n₂ sinθ₂.** Refractive index n = c/v. Total internal reflection above the critical angle.
**Thin lens/mirror: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u** (signs by convention). Magnification m = −v/u.
**Doppler effect:** observed frequency shifts up as a source approaches, down as it recedes. Basis of radar, sirens and cosmic redshift.
**E = mc²** — mass and energy are equivalent; a tiny mass holds enormous energy (c² ≈ 9×10¹⁶). Total energy E² = (pc)² + (mc²)².
**Photon energy E = hf = hc/λ**, h = 6.626×10⁻³⁴ J·s. Light is quantised into photons (Planck/Einstein).
**de Broglie wavelength λ = h/p** — every particle has a wave nature. Foundation of wave–particle duality and quantum mechanics.
**Heisenberg uncertainty: Δx·Δp ≥ ℏ/2.** You can't know position and momentum exactly at once — a fundamental limit, not a measurement flaw.
The **Schrödinger equation** governs how a quantum wavefunction ψ evolves; |ψ|² gives the probability of finding the particle. Time-independent: Ĥψ = Eψ.
**Photoelectric effect:** light above a threshold frequency ejects electrons; energy **KE_max = hf − φ** (φ = work function). Won Einstein the Nobel; proved light quanta.
**Special relativity:** moving clocks run slow (time dilation) and lengths contract, by the Lorentz factor **γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²)**. The speed of light is the same for all observers.

**General relativity:** gravity is the curvature of spacetime by mass-energy (Einstein's field equations). Predicts black holes, gravitational lensing, time running slower in stronger gravity, and gravitational waves.
**Kepler's laws:** 1) orbits are ellipses with the Sun at a focus; 2) equal areas in equal times; 3) **T² ∝ a³**.
**Hubble's law: v = H₀·d** — galaxies recede faster the farther they are; the universe is expanding (H₀ ≈ 70 km/s/Mpc).
**Blackbody radiation:** power **P = σAT⁴** (Stefan–Boltzmann, σ = 5.67×10⁻⁸); peak wavelength λ_max = b/T (Wien's law). Hotter = brighter and bluer.
**Four fundamental forces:** gravity (weakest, infinite range), electromagnetism, the **strong** nuclear force (binds quarks/nuclei), and the **weak** force (radioactive decay).
**Standard Model:** matter is built from 6 **quarks** and 6 **leptons** (incl. the electron); forces are carried by **bosons** (photon, gluon, W/Z), with the **Higgs** giving mass.
**Pressure P = F/A** (pascals). In a fluid: P = ρgh. **Archimedes:** buoyant force = weight of fluid displaced. Bernoulli: faster flow = lower pressure.
**Torque τ = rF sinθ** — the rotational analogue of force. Angular momentum **L = Iω**, conserved when no external torque acts.
**Friction: f = μN.** Static (μ_s, before sliding) is larger than kinetic (μ_k, while sliding); it always opposes motion.
**Hooke's law: F = −kx** — restoring force ∝ extension (k = stiffness). Stored PE = ½kx², valid up to the elastic limit.
**Projectile motion:** horizontal and vertical motions are independent. Range R = v²sin(2θ)/g, max height H = v²sin²θ/(2g), flight time 2v sinθ/g. Max range at 45°.
**Escape velocity v = √(2GM/r)** (Earth ≈ 11.2 km/s); circular orbit v = √(GM/r). Gravitational PE U = −GMm/r.

**Rotational dynamics:** τ = Iα (the rotational F=ma). **Moment of inertia I = Σmr²** (disc ½MR², solid sphere ⅖MR², rod 1/12·ML²). Rotational KE = ½Iω²; **angular momentum L = Iω**, conserved without external torque.
**Angular kinematics:** ω = ω₀ + αt, θ = ω₀t + ½αt². Link to linear: v = rω, a = rα. Mirrors SUVAT.
**Fluid flow:** continuity **A₁v₁ = A₂v₂** (mass conserved). **Bernoulli: P + ½ρv² + ρgh = constant** — faster flow means lower pressure (wing lift, venturi, spray guns).

**Viscosity & turbulence:** viscous drag resists flow. **Reynolds number Re = ρvL/μ** predicts laminar (low) vs turbulent (high) flow. Stokes drag on a sphere F = 6πμrv — relevant to mixing and pumping cleaners.
**Thermal expansion:** linear ΔL = αLΔT (area ≈2α, volume ≈3α). Why pipes, bridges and bottles need slack.
**Heat transfer, three ways:** **conduction** (Q/t = kAΔT/d, Fourier), **convection** (bulk fluid motion), and **radiation** (P = σAT⁴). Drives drying and reactor temperature control.
**Kinetic theory:** average molecular KE = (3/2)k_BT; **rms speed v = √(3k_BT/m)**. Temperature *is* molecular motion.
**Thermodynamic processes:** isothermal (T const → PV const), **adiabatic (Q=0 → PV^γ const)**, isobaric (P const), isochoric (V const). γ = Cp/Cv.
**Statistical entropy: S = k_B·ln Ω** (Boltzmann) — entropy counts the microstates of a system. Links heat to probability.
**Gauss's law: ∮E·dA = Q_enclosed/ε₀** — total electric flux through a closed surface depends only on the charge inside. One of Maxwell's four.
**Kirchhoff's laws:** current law (Σ in = Σ out at a node — charge conserved); voltage law (Σ voltages around a loop = 0 — energy conserved).
**RC circuit:** charge/discharge is exponential with **time constant τ = RC** — ~63% after one τ, essentially complete after 5τ.
**AC circuits:** V = V₀sin(ωt), **RMS = peak/√2**. Reactance: capacitor X_C = 1/(ωC), inductor X_L = ωL; impedance Z combines R and X. Resonance at ω = 1/√(LC).
**Inductance:** EMF = −L(dI/dt); energy stored E = ½LI². An inductor resists changes in current.
**Magnetic field sources:** straight wire B = μ₀I/(2πr); solenoid B = μ₀nI. **Ampère's law:** ∮B·dl = μ₀I; Biot–Savart for any shape. μ₀ = 4π×10⁻⁷.
**EM spectrum** (long→short λ): radio, microwave, infrared, visible (400–700 nm), ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma. All travel at c; photon energy E = hf grows as λ shrinks.
**Interference & diffraction:** double-slit maxima at **d·sinθ = mλ**; single-slit minima at a·sinθ = mλ; a grating disperses light by wavelength. Proof that light is a wave.
**Polarisation — Malus's law: I = I₀·cos²θ** for light through a polariser at angle θ. Used in LCD screens and polarised sunglasses.
**Standing waves:** on a string (or open pipe) harmonics are **f_n = n·v/(2L)**; a pipe closed at one end gives odd harmonics f_n = n·v/(4L).
**Sound level: β = 10·log(I/I₀) dB** (I₀ = 10⁻¹² W/m²); +10 dB = 10× intensity. Two close frequencies produce **beats** at |f₁−f₂|.
**Bohr model:** electron energy **E_n = −13.6/n² eV**; jumps emit/absorb photons. Orbit radius r_n = n²·0.529 Å.
**Atomic spectra — Rydberg: 1/λ = R(1/n₁² − 1/n₂²)**, R = 1.097×10⁷ m⁻¹. Explains hydrogen's Balmer/Lyman lines.
**Particle in a box:** E_n = n²h²/(8mL²) — confinement quantises energy; a smaller box spreads the levels. Basis of quantum dots.

**Quantum numbers** (n, l, m_l, m_s) label electron states; **Pauli exclusion** forbids two electrons sharing all four — the reason atoms have shells and the periodic table has structure. Electrons are spin-½ fermions.
**Quantum tunnelling:** a particle can cross a barrier it classically couldn't; probability falls exponentially with width. Powers stellar fusion, STMs and flash memory.
**Nuclear binding energy** comes from the **mass defect: E = Δm·c²**. Iron-56 is the most tightly bound — fusion of lighter nuclei and fission of heavier ones both release energy.
**Radioactive decay: N = N₀·e^(−λt)**; **half-life t½ = ln2/λ**; activity A = λN. Independent of temperature or chemistry.
**Decay modes:** alpha (emits a He nucleus), beta (n→p + electron + antineutrino, or the reverse), gamma (high-energy photon). Charge and nucleon number are conserved.
**Fission:** a heavy nucleus (U-235) splits, releasing energy and neutrons → chain reaction. **Fusion:** light nuclei merge into helium — the Sun's engine, far more energy per kg.
**Relativistic dynamics:** p = γmv, E = γmc², and **E² = (pc)² + (mc²)²**. As v→c energy →∞, so nothing with mass reaches light speed.
**Relativistic velocity addition: w = (u+v)/(1 + uv/c²)** — velocities don't simply add, and the result never exceeds c.
**Equivalence principle:** locally, gravity is indistinguishable from acceleration — the idea that grew into general relativity.
**Black holes:** inside the **event horizon** (radius r_s = 2GM/c², Schwarzschild) escape velocity exceeds c. **Hawking radiation** lets them slowly evaporate.

**Cosmology:** the universe began ~13.8 billion years ago (**Big Bang**), leaving the cosmic microwave background. It's ~68% **dark energy**, ~27% **dark matter**, ~5% ordinary matter — and expanding faster over time.
**Lagrangian mechanics (advanced): L = T − V.** Real paths extremise the action ∫L dt, giving the **Euler–Lagrange equation** d/dt(∂L/∂q̇) − ∂L/∂q = 0 — all of mechanics from one function.
**Hamiltonian mechanics: H = T + V** in terms of position q and momentum p; evolution by q̇ = ∂H/∂p, ṗ = −∂H/∂q. The natural bridge into quantum mechanics.
**Noether's theorem:** every continuous symmetry yields a conservation law — time-symmetry → energy, space → momentum, rotation → angular momentum. One of physics' deepest truths.

**Statistical mechanics:** the **partition function Z = Σe^(−E/k_BT)** generates all thermodynamics; states follow the Boltzmann factor. Quantum statistics: **Fermi–Dirac** (fermions), **Bose–Einstein** (bosons), Maxwell–Boltzmann (classical).
**Quantum formalism:** observables are operators; the canonical commutator **[x,p] = iℏ** forces the uncertainty relation. Expectation ⟨A⟩ = ⟨ψ|Â|ψ⟩; measurement collapses ψ onto an eigenstate.

**Quantum field theory (advanced):** particles are excitations of fields. **QED** (the EM force via virtual photons, drawn as Feynman diagrams) is the most precisely tested theory in science; the Standard Model is a QFT.

**Solid-state:** electrons fill **energy bands**; a **band gap** separates conductors (no gap), semiconductors (small — Si, Ge) and insulators (large). Doping makes n-/p-type; junctions make diodes and transistors.
**Superconductivity:** below a critical temperature resistance vanishes and magnetic fields are expelled (Meissner effect), explained by Cooper-pair formation (BCS theory).
**Hall effect:** a magnetic field across a current-carrying strip creates a transverse voltage V_H = IB/(nqt), revealing carrier type and density.
**Dimensional analysis:** every term in an equation must share units. Checking dimensions catches mistakes and can even derive a relationship up to a constant.
**Quadratic formula:** for ax²+bx+c=0, **x = (−b ± √(b²−4ac)) / 2a**. The discriminant b²−4ac tells you: >0 two real roots, =0 one, <0 complex.
**Pythagoras: a² + b² = c²** — in a right triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the other two squares.

**Derivative** = instantaneous rate of change/slope. Power rule **d/dx[xⁿ] = nxⁿ⁻¹**. Product: (uv)' = u'v+uv'. Quotient and **chain rule** (f(g))' = f'(g)·g'. d/dx[eˣ]=eˣ, d/dx[ln x]=1/x, d/dx[sin x]=cos x.
**Integration** = area under a curve / antiderivative. ∫xⁿ dx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n+1) + C. **Fundamental Theorem of Calculus:** ∫ₐᵇ f'(x)dx = f(b) − f(a).
A **limit** is the value a function approaches. For 0/0 or ∞/∞, **L'Hôpital's rule:** lim f/g = lim f'/g'.
**Taylor series:** f(x) = Σ fⁿ(a)/n! · (x−a)ⁿ. e.g. eˣ = 1 + x + x²/2! + x³/3! + …; sin x = x − x³/3! + x⁵/5! − …
**Trig identities:** sin²θ+cos²θ=1; sin(A±B)=sinA cosB ± cosA sinB; cos(A±B)=cosA cosB ∓ sinA sinB; double angle sin2θ=2sinθcosθ, cos2θ=cos²θ−sin²θ.
**Law of sines:** a/sinA = b/sinB = c/sinC. **Law of cosines:** c² = a² + b² − 2ab·cosC (generalised Pythagoras).
**Logs:** log(xy)=log x+log y; log(x/y)=log x−log y; log(xⁿ)=n log x; change of base log_b x = ln x/ln b. **Exponents:** xᵃ·xᵇ=xᵃ⁺ᵇ, (xᵃ)ᵇ=xᵃᵇ, x⁰=1.
**Binomial theorem:** (a+b)ⁿ = Σ C(n,k)·aⁿ⁻ᵏbᵏ. Coefficients are Pascal's triangle / C(n,k)=n!/(k!(n−k)!).
**Arithmetic:** aₙ = a₁+(n−1)d, sum Sₙ = n/2·(a₁+aₙ). **Geometric:** aₙ = a₁rⁿ⁻¹, sum Sₙ = a₁(1−rⁿ)/(1−r); infinite (|r|<1) = a₁/(1−r).
**Areas:** circle πr², triangle ½bh, rectangle lw. **Volumes:** sphere 4/3·πr³, cylinder πr²h, cone 1/3·πr²h, box lwh. Circle circumference 2πr.
**Matrices:** multiply row×column (AB exists if cols(A)=rows(B), not commutative). 2×2 **determinant** = ad−bc; inverse = 1/det·[[d,−b],[−c,a]]. Used for transformations and solving linear systems.
The **determinant** scales area/volume under a matrix transform; det=0 means the matrix is singular (no inverse). 2×2: ad−bc.
**Eigenvalues/eigenvectors:** for Av = λv, v is an eigenvector and λ its eigenvalue — directions a matrix only stretches, not rotates. Found from det(A−λI)=0.
**Vectors:** **dot product** a·b = |a||b|cosθ (scalar, 0 if perpendicular); **cross product** a×b = |a||b|sinθ (vector ⟂ to both, right-hand rule).
**Probability** P(A) ∈ [0,1]. P(A or B) = P(A)+P(B)−P(A and B). Independent: P(A and B)=P(A)P(B). Complement P(not A)=1−P(A).
**Bayes' theorem: P(A|B) = P(B|A)·P(A) / P(B).** Updates a belief given new evidence — the engine behind a lot of inference and ML.
**Permutations** (order matters): P(n,r)=n!/(n−r)!. **Combinations** (order not): C(n,r)=n!/(r!(n−r)!).
**Stats:** mean = sum/n; median = middle value; mode = most frequent. **Variance** = average squared deviation; **standard deviation** σ = √variance (spread).
**Normal distribution** (bell curve): symmetric about the mean; **68–95–99.7%** of data fall within 1/2/3 σ. **z-score = (x−μ)/σ** standardises a value.
**Central Limit Theorem:** the mean of many independent samples is approximately **normally distributed**, whatever the original distribution — why the bell curve is everywhere.
**Expected value E[X] = Σ x·P(x)** — the long-run average of a random variable. Core to betting, risk and decision-making.
**Primes** have exactly two divisors (2,3,5,7,11…); every integer factors uniquely into primes. **GCD** = largest common divisor (Euclid's algorithm); LCM = smallest common multiple.
**Modular arithmetic:** numbers wrap around a modulus (like a clock). a ≡ b (mod n) means n divides (a−b). Backbone of cryptography.
**Factorial n! = n·(n−1)·…·1** (0! = 1). Counts orderings of n items; grows extremely fast.
**Euler's identity: e^(iπ) + 1 = 0** — linking e, i, π, 1 and 0. Often called the most beautiful equation in mathematics. From e^(iθ)=cosθ+i·sinθ.
**Constants:** π ≈ 3.14159 (circle), e ≈ 2.71828 (natural growth), φ ≈ 1.61803 (golden ratio), i = √(−1) (imaginary unit).
A **differential equation** relates a function to its derivatives (e.g. dy/dx = ky → exponential growth y=Ce^(kx)). Models populations, decay, motion, circuits.
**Line: y = mx + c** — m is slope (rise/run), c the y-intercept. Slope between points = (y₂−y₁)/(x₂−x₁).
**Percent:** part/whole×100. **% change = (new−old)/old×100.** Compound growth: final = initial·(1+r)ⁿ.
**Complex numbers z = a + bi** (i² = −1). Modulus |z| = √(a²+b²), argument θ = atan2(b,a); polar z = r·e^(iθ). **De Moivre:** (r·e^(iθ))ⁿ = rⁿ·e^(inθ).
**Fibonacci:** 0,1,1,2,3,5,8,13,… each term the sum of the two before (Fₙ = Fₙ₋₁ + Fₙ₋₂). The ratio of consecutive terms → the golden ratio φ ≈ 1.618.
**Fourier:** any periodic signal is a sum of sines/cosines; the **Fourier transform F(ω) = ∫f(t)e^(−iωt)dt** moves between time and frequency. The heart of audio, imaging and signal processing.
**Laplace transform: F(s) = ∫₀^∞ f(t)e^(−st)dt** — turns differential equations into algebra. The standard tool for circuits and control systems.
**Partial derivatives** ∂f/∂x vary one variable, holding the rest fixed. The **gradient ∇f** points in the direction of steepest increase — central to optimisation and ML.
**Vector calculus operators:** **divergence ∇·F** (net source), **curl ∇×F** (local rotation), **Laplacian ∇²f** (curvature). The building blocks of physics PDEs.
**Multiple integrals** (∬, ∭) integrate over areas and volumes. Changing variables multiplies by the **Jacobian** determinant; polar/spherical coordinates tame symmetry.

**The big vector-calculus theorems** — **Green's**, **Stokes'** and the **Divergence (Gauss) theorem** — each relate an integral over a region to one over its boundary, generalising the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.
**Series convergence tests:** **ratio** (lim|aₙ₊₁/aₙ| < 1 ⇒ converges), root, comparison, integral, and alternating-series. A geometric series converges iff |r| < 1.
**Power series Σ cₙ(x−a)ⁿ** converge within a **radius of convergence** R (from the ratio test); Taylor and Maclaurin series are special cases.
**First-order ODEs:** separable (∫dy/g(y) = ∫f(x)dx) and linear y′ + P(x)y = Q(x), solved with the **integrating factor** e^(∫P dx).
**Second-order linear ODEs** ay″ + by′ + cy = 0: solve the **characteristic equation** ar² + br + c = 0 — real roots → exponentials, complex roots → oscillation (springs, RLC circuits).
**PDEs** govern fields: the **heat** equation (diffusion), the **wave** equation, and **Laplace's** equation ∇²u = 0. Solved by separation of variables / Fourier methods.
**Newton's method** finds roots: x_{n+1} = xₙ − f(xₙ)/f′(xₙ). Near a root it roughly doubles the correct digits each step.
**Proof techniques:** direct, **contradiction** (assume the negation), **induction** (base case + inductive step), contrapositive, and counterexample.
**Number theory:** **Fermat's little theorem** a^(p−1) ≡ 1 (mod p) for prime p; **Euler's totient φ(n)** counts coprime integers; modular inverses + these underpin **RSA encryption**.

**Group theory (abstract algebra):** a **group** is a set with an operation that is closed, associative, has an identity and inverses. Rings add a second operation; **fields** (ℝ, ℂ, ℚ) allow division. The language of symmetry.
**Graph theory:** vertices joined by edges. An **Euler path** uses every edge once (exists iff ≤2 odd-degree vertices); a tree is connected and acyclic. Models networks, routes and circuits.
**Counting tools:** **pigeonhole** (n+1 items in n boxes ⇒ a repeat), **inclusion–exclusion** (|A∪B| = |A|+|B|−|A∩B|), and the multiplication principle.
**Binomial distribution:** n independent trials with success prob p → P(k) = C(n,k)·pᵏ(1−p)ⁿ⁻ᵏ; mean np, variance np(1−p).
**Poisson distribution:** rare events at average rate λ → P(k) = λᵏe^(−λ)/k!; mean = variance = λ. Models arrivals, defects and calls.
**Continuous distributions:** **uniform** (flat), **exponential** (waiting times, λe^(−λx), memoryless), and the normal/Gaussian. Each has a PDF whose area = probability.
**Covariance** measures joint variation; **correlation r = cov(X,Y)/(σ_Xσ_Y) ∈ [−1,1]** normalises it. |r| near 1 = strong linear link — but correlation isn't causation.
**Hypothesis testing:** assume H₀, compute a statistic and a **p-value**; if p < α (often 0.05), reject H₀. Beware type I (false positive) and type II errors.
**Confidence interval:** a range likely to hold the true value — e.g. mean ± 1.96·(σ/√n) for 95%. It narrows as the sample grows.
**Linear regression (least squares):** fit y = mx + c by minimising squared residuals; **R²** is the fraction of variance explained. The base of predictive modelling.

**Markov chains:** the next state depends only on the current one (memoryless). A transition matrix evolves the probabilities, often settling to a stationary distribution. Behind PageRank and much of ML.
**Gradient descent:** to minimise f, step downhill **x ← x − η·∇f** (η = learning rate). The workhorse of training neural networks.
**Lagrange multipliers:** to optimise f subject to g = 0, solve **∇f = λ∇g**. Finds constrained maxima/minima across economics, ML and physics.

**Linear programming:** maximise a linear objective under linear constraints; the optimum lies at a vertex of the feasible region (simplex method). Core to logistics and operations — useful for your fleet phase.
**Game theory:** players pick strategies; a **Nash equilibrium** is a state where no one gains by changing alone. Models markets, pricing, auctions and negotiation.
**Conic sections:** circle x²+y²=r², **ellipse** x²/a²+y²/b²=1, **parabola** y=ax², **hyperbola** x²/a²−y²/b²=1 — the shapes of orbits, dishes and lenses.
**Hyperbolic functions:** sinh x = (eˣ−e⁻ˣ)/2, cosh x = (eˣ+e⁻ˣ)/2, with cosh²−sinh² = 1. They describe hanging cables (catenaries) and relativity.
**Polar coordinates** (r,θ): x = r cosθ, y = r sinθ. **Parametric** curves give x(t), y(t) — natural for motion and spirals.
**Mean Value Theorem:** a smooth curve has a point where the instantaneous slope equals the average slope over [a,b]; Rolle's theorem is the equal-endpoints case.
**Key inequalities:** triangle |a+b| ≤ |a|+|b|; **Cauchy–Schwarz** |⟨a,b⟩| ≤ ‖a‖·‖b‖; AM–GM (arithmetic mean ≥ geometric mean).

**Linear algebra core:** vectors are **linearly independent** if none is a combination of the others; a **basis** spans the space with the fewest vectors, and its size is the **dimension**. Rank = number of independent columns.
**Solving linear systems:** Gaussian elimination row-reduces to triangular form; or Ax = b ⇒ x = A⁻¹b when A is invertible. **Cramer's rule** expresses each unknown as a ratio of determinants.
**Sets & infinity (Cantor):** some infinities are larger than others — the integers are countable, the reals uncountable. A set's power set is always strictly bigger.
**Gödel's incompleteness:** any consistent system rich enough for arithmetic contains true statements it cannot prove — a hard limit on formal mathematics.
**Famous open problems:** the **Riemann hypothesis** (zeros of the zeta function), **P vs NP**, and others — the Millennium Prize problems, $1M each. The live frontier of maths.
**Growth models:** exponential dy/dt = ky → y = y₀eᵏᵗ; **logistic** dy/dt = ky(1−y/K) levels off at carrying capacity K (populations, product adoption, your market sizing).

**Free Fire** is a mobile battle-royale by Garena - 48-50 players drop on an island, loot weapons and fight to be the last squad standing in ~10-minute matches. It's the heart of your AyerFire brand and JD Esports Arena tournaments, Prabin.

**Battle Royale (BR):** many players, one shrinking safe-zone, last one alive wins. In Free Fire it's squads of 4 on Bermuda/Purgatory/Kalahari - rotate with the zone, hold high ground, watch for third-party fights.
**Clash Squad** is Free Fire's 4v4 round-based mode: buy weapons each round with in-game cash, best of 7. Fast, aim-heavy, and the format most ranked grinders use to sharpen up.

**Free Fire characters** have active/passive skills. Popular picks: **DJ Alok** (heal + speed aura), **Chrono** (force-field shield), **K/Kelly** (EP conversion / sprint). Match the skill to your role - rusher, support or sniper.
**Free Fire ranked tiers:** Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond, Heroic, then **Grandmaster** (top). You climb with placement + kills; Grandmaster is a fixed-slot leaderboard each season.

k: how to be pro free fire
facts.a: **Get better at Free Fire, Prabin:** lock one sensitivity and stop changing it; drill drag-headshots in training daily; learn rotations and zone timing; play Clash Squad for raw aim; review your own clips for mistakes. Consistency beats binge-grinding.

**Free Fire sensitivity** is personal, but a common base: General and Red Dot high, scopes a touch lower, with a 2-3 finger claw HUD so you can move, fire and scope at once. Tune until your headshot drag is repeatable, then leave it alone.
**Free Fire pets** give passive bonuses (faster EP gain, reduced skill cooldowns, etc.). Pick a pet that complements your character's skill rather than the flashiest one.

**Diamonds** are Free Fire's premium currency for skins, characters and the Elite Pass. Top up only through official Garena channels or authorised resellers - third-party 'free diamond' sites are scams and get accounts banned.

k: free fire max vs free fire
facts.a: **Free Fire MAX** is the higher-graphics build of the same game with shared accounts and lobbies (Firelink). Same matches, better visuals - and on a capable emulator it can hit much higher FPS, which you've tuned before.

**Minecraft** is a sandbox game of breaking and placing blocks in a procedurally generated world - build anything, survive the night, explore caves and other dimensions. Yours runs on the Aternos server (Ogsssss.aternos.me).

**Survival** = gather resources, manage health/hunger, fight mobs, progress through gear tiers. **Creative** = unlimited blocks, flight, no damage - pure building. Most multiplayer servers run Survival for the challenge.
**Crafting** turns materials into tools and blocks via a recipe grid; a **crafting table** unlocks the full 3x3 grid. Core early path: wood, planks, sticks, wooden tools, stone tools, then iron.
**Creeper** - the green mob that sneaks up and explodes, wrecking builds and gear. Don't face-tank it: hit and step back, or keep a cat nearby (creepers flee cats and ocelots).
**Hostile mobs** spawn in the dark: zombies, skeletons (bows), creepers, spiders, endermen. Light your base with torches to stop spawns, and carry a shield against skeletons.
**Redstone** is Minecraft's wiring - power, logic gates, pistons, doors and contraptions. It's basically in-game electrical engineering: signals, repeaters, comparators and circuits.

**The Nether** is the fiery dimension reached through an obsidian portal - source of blaze rods, quartz and netherite, plus fast overworld travel (1 block = 8 above). Bring fire resistance and mind the lava.

**The End** is the final dimension where you fight the **Ender Dragon** - break the end crystals on the pillars first, then burst it down. Beating it 'finishes' the game and opens End cities (elytra wings).
**Enchanting** upgrades gear with XP + lapis at an enchanting table (more bookshelves around it = stronger options). Key ones: Protection, Sharpness, Efficiency, Unbreaking, Mending.
**Villagers** trade goods for emeralds by profession (farmer, librarian, armorer...). A trading hall turns surplus into emeralds, enchanted books and gear.
**Biomes** are world regions with their own terrain, mobs and resources - plains, desert, jungle, taiga, ocean, mushroom fields. They shape what you find and build with.

**Aternos** is a free Minecraft server host - easy and great for friends, but servers **sleep when empty** and it bans keep-alive/AFK bots. For true 24/7 you need a paid host or a free always-on VM like Oracle Cloud, Prabin.

**Always-on Minecraft, Prabin:** a free **Oracle Cloud 'Always Free' ARM VM** can run a server 24/7 (you set it up yourself), or a cheap paid host (~$3-8/mo) gives one-click uptime. Aternos has no legit 24/7 mode and no allowed bot.
**Diamonds** spawn deep (around Y -59 in current versions). Branch-mine at that level with an iron pickaxe, watch for lava, and bring torches and food.
**Esports** is competitive video gaming - organised tournaments, teams, prize pools and audiences. Your JD Esports Arena is grassroots esports: hosting Free Fire competition in Nepal.

**FPS (frames per second)** is how many images per second your screen draws - higher = smoother and faster reactions. 60 is fine, 90-120+ feels noticeably crisper; you've pushed Free Fire MAX to high FPS on emulator.

**Ping/latency** is the round-trip delay (ms) to the server - lower is better. Under ~50ms feels instant; high ping causes rubber-banding and 'shot first but died'. Wired internet and a nearby server help most.
**DPI** is mouse sensitivity (dots per inch) - higher moves your aim more per motion. Most FPS players sit around 400-800 DPI and tune in-game sensitivity for control, not raw speed.

**To improve aim:** train daily in a mode that isolates it (Clash Squad, training grounds, or a PC aim trainer), keep one sensitivity, focus on crosshair placement at head height, and warm up before ranked. Reps and consistency win.
